1: # Irreducibility after reduction of an admissible sl2 lattice
2: 
3: ## Original exercise
4: 
5: James E. Humphreys, *Introduction to Lie Algebras and Representation Theory*,
6: Graduate Texts in Mathematics 9, Springer, section 27, exercise 7,
7: printed page 164. The exercise-list convention on page 163 sets
8: \(L=\mathfrak{sl}_2\) and identifies weights with integers.
9: Book DOI: [10.1007/978-1-4612-6398-2](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4612-6398-2).
10: 
11: > 7. If \(0\leq\lambda<\operatorname{char}K\), \(V=V(\lambda)\),
12: > prove that \(V(K)\) is irreducible as \(L(K)\)-module.
13: 
14: ## Definitions and complete target
15: 
16: Let \(p\) be any prime, \(K\) any field of characteristic \(p\), and
17: \(\lambda\) an integer with \(0\leq\lambda<p\).
18: Let \(V(\lambda)\) be the complex irreducible highest-weight
19: \(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\)-module of highest weight \(\lambda\),
20: of dimension \(\lambda+1\). Its Chevalley generators satisfy
21: 
22: \[
23: [h,x]=2x,\qquad[h,y]=-2y,\qquad[x,y]=h.
24: \]
25: 
26: Choose a nonzero highest-weight vector \(v\) with \(xv=0\) and
27: \(hv=\lambda v\). Let \(U_{\mathbb Z}\) be the integer subalgebra of
28: the universal enveloping algebra generated by all divided powers
29: \(X_r=x^r/r!\), \(Y_r=y^r/r!\), for integers \(r\geq0\).
30: An **admissible lattice** \(M\subset V(\lambda)\) is a free abelian
31: subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis, stable under
32: \(U_{\mathbb Z}\). It is arbitrary, not necessarily the minimal lattice.
33: 
34: Put \(V(K)=M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\). The Lie algebra
35: \(L(K)=(\mathbb Zx+\mathbb Zy+\mathbb Zh)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\)
36: acts by the induced lattice operators. This is the Chevalley
37: \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) construction also in characteristic 2.
38: Prove that \(V(K)\) is nonzero and every \(K\)-linear subspace
39: invariant under \(x,y,h\) is zero or all of \(V(K)\).
40: Both \(\lambda=0\) and \(p=2\) are included; \(K\) need not be
41: algebraically closed.
42: 
43: ## Fixed natural-language proof
44: 
45: ### 1. Divided-power coordinates in characteristic zero
46: 
47: Put \(n=\lambda+1\) and \(e_i=y^iv/i!\) for \(0\leq i\leq\lambda\).
48: The commutator identities give, by induction,
49: 
50: \[
51: hy^iv=(\lambda-2i)y^iv,\qquad
52: xy^iv=i(\lambda-i+1)y^{i-1}v\quad(i\geq1).
53: \]
54: 
55: For \(i\leq\lambda\), applying \(x^i\) to \(y^iv\) gives
56: \(i!\lambda(\lambda-1)\cdots(\lambda-i+1)v\ne0\) over \(\mathbb C\).
57: At \(i=0\) the empty product is one. Thus every \(e_i\ne0\).
58: Their \(h\)-eigenvalues \(\lambda-2i\) are distinct over \(\mathbb C\),
59: so they are linearly independent: applying
60: \(\prod_{k\ne j}(h-(\lambda-2k)\mathrm{Id})\) to a relation isolates
61: its \(j\)-th coefficient with a nonzero multiplier.
62: There are \(n\) vectors, the dimension of \(V(\lambda)\), hence they
63: form a basis. Also \(y^{\lambda+1}v=0\), since otherwise it would be
64: an eigenvector of eigenvalue \(-\lambda-2\), absent from this basis.
65: All higher lowering powers vanish as well.
66: 
67: The operator matrices are therefore
68: 
69: \[
70: xe_0=0,\quad xe_i=(\lambda-i+1)e_{i-1}\ (i\geq1),\qquad
71: ye_i=(i+1)e_{i+1}\ (i<\lambda),\quad ye_\lambda=0,
72: \quad he_i=(\lambda-2i)e_i.
73: \]
74: 
75: Iteration gives the integral divided-power matrices
76: 
77: \[
78: X_re_i=\binom{\lambda-i+r}{r}e_{i-r}\quad(0\leq r\leq i),
79: \qquad
80: Y_re_i=\binom{i+r}{r}e_{i+r}\quad(i+r\leq\lambda).       \tag{1}
81: \]
82: 
83: The respective expressions are zero when \(r>i\) or
84: \(i+r>\lambda\), by termination of the strings just proved.
85: 
86: ### 2. Matrix units preserve the localized arbitrary lattice
87: 
88: Let \(R=\mathbb Z_{(p)}=\{a/b\in\mathbb Q:p\nmid b\}\), and regard
89: \(M_R=R\otimes_{\mathbb Z}M\) as a submodule of \(V(\lambda)\).
90: The embedding is injective because an integer basis of \(M\) is
91: complex-linearly independent. The module \(M_R\) is free of rank \(n\)
92: over \(R\) and is preserved by all \(X_r,Y_r\), by admissibility.
93: 
94: Define \(E_{ij}\) to send \(e_j\) to \(e_i\) and all other basis
95: vectors to zero. Formula (1) gives
96: 
97: \[
98: P:=Y_\lambda X_\lambda=E_{\lambda\lambda},\qquad
99: X_{\lambda-i}P=E_{i\lambda},\qquad
100: P Y_{\lambda-j}=\binom\lambda j E_{\lambda j}.
101: \]
102: 
103: For the last identity, an input index below \(j\) is sent below
104: \(e_\lambda\) and killed by \(P\); an index above \(j\) is sent past
105: the end of the lowering string. On \(e_j\) the coefficient is precisely
106: \(\binom\lambda j\). Since \(\lambda<p\), none of
107: \(\lambda!\), \(j!\), \((\lambda-j)!\) is divisible by \(p\), so
108: \(\binom\lambda j\) is a unit in \(R\). Consequently
109: 
110: \[
111: E_{ij}=\left(\binom\lambda j\right)^{-1}
112:        X_{\lambda-i}P Y_{\lambda-j}.                 \tag{2}
113: \]
114: 
115: Every matrix unit preserves \(M_R\). No assertion about distinct
116: weights modulo \(p\) has been used.
117: 
118: ### 3. Recover a standard basis for the arbitrary lattice
119: 
120: Define \(J_i=\{c\in\mathbb C:c e_i\in M_R\}\).
121: The coordinate projection \(E_{ii}\) maps \(M_R\) onto \(J_i e_i\).
122: Applying \(E_{ij}\) to \(c e_j\) shows \(J_j\subseteq J_i\);
123: reversing the indices gives equality. Let \(J\) be their common module.
124: It is finitely generated, being a projection of a finite free module,
125: and nonzero because \(M_R\) spans \(V(\lambda)\) over \(\mathbb C\).
126: The coordinate projections and independence of the \(e_i\) give
127: 
128: \[
129: M_R=\bigoplus_{i=0}^{\lambda}J e_i.                  \tag{3}
130: \]
131: 
132: One must still prove that \(J\) has rank one; containment in
133: \(\mathbb C\) alone does not imply that. Let
134: \(r=\dim_{\mathbb Q}(\mathbb Q\otimes_R J)\), which is finite.
135: Tensoring (3) with the fraction field \(\mathbb Q\) and using the
136: rank \(n\) of \(M_R\) gives \(n=nr\), so \(r=1\), since \(n>0\).
137: The multiplication map \(\mathbb Q\otimes_R J\to\mathbb C\) is
138: injective: this tensor product is the localization of the torsion-free
139: module \(J\subset\mathbb C\), and a fraction mapping to zero has
140: zero numerator. Thus \(J\) spans a one-dimensional rational line.
141: 
142: Choose \(0\ne a\in J\) and write a finite set of nonzero generators
143: as \(q_1a,\ldots,q_ka\) with \(q_j\in\mathbb Q^\times\).
144: Each \(q_j=p^{\nu_j}u_j\) for \(\nu_j\in\mathbb Z\) and a unit
145: \(u_j\) of \(R\). Let \(\nu=\min_j\nu_j\). All generators belong
146: to \(p^\nu R a\), and a generator with minimal exponent generates
147: that whole module. Therefore \(J=Rb\) for a nonzero \(b\in J\).
148: By (3), \(b e_0,\ldots,b e_\lambda\) is an \(R\)-basis of \(M_R\).
149: 
150: ### 4. Reduce and extend scalars
151: 
152: All denominators in \(R\) are invertible in \(K\), so the integer map
153: extends to \(R\to K\). The natural tensor maps give
154: 
155: \[
156: M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\cong M_R\otimes_R K
157: \cong(M_R/pM_R)\otimes_{\mathbb F_p}K.
158: \]
159: 
160: For example the first map sends \(m\otimes c\) to
161: \((1\otimes m)\otimes c\); its inverse sends
162: \((r\otimes m)\otimes c\) to \(m\otimes\bar r c\).
163: The reduced images \(b_0,\ldots,b_\lambda\) of \(b e_i\) form a
164: \(K\)-basis, with exactly the matrices of step 1 reduced into \(K\).
165: The matrix-unit identities (2) persist on this basis.
166: 
167: For \(0\leq r\leq\lambda<p\), \(r!\ne0\) in \(K\), and the induced
168: \(X_r,Y_r\) equal \((r!)^{-1}x^r,(r!)^{-1}y^r\). Hence any
169: \(K\)-subspace invariant under \(x,y\) is invariant under every matrix
170: unit in (2).
171: 
172: ### 5. Conclude irreducibility
173: 
174: Let \(W\) be invariant. If it is nonzero, choose
175: \(0\ne w=\sum_i c_i b_i\in W\), and an index \(j\) with \(c_j\ne0\).
176: For every \(i\), \(E_{ij}w=c_jb_i\in W\). Division by \(c_j\)
177: gives \(b_i\in W\), so all basis vectors lie in \(W\) and
178: \(W=V(K)\). Since \(\dim_K V(K)=\lambda+1>0\), it is nonzero and
179: irreducible. If \(\lambda=0\), all relevant factorials and binomial
180: coefficients are one and the argument applies unchanged. For \(p=2\),

5: library searches and individual background notes are available on demand;

Let \(p\) be any prime, \(K\) any field of characteristic \(p\), and
\(\lambda\) an integer with \(0\leq\lambda<p\).
Let \(V(\lambda)\) be the complex irreducible highest-weight
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\)-module of highest weight \(\lambda\),
of dimension \(\lambda+1\). Its Chevalley generators satisfy

\[
[h,x]=2x,\qquad[h,y]=-2y,\qquad[x,y]=h.
\]

Choose a nonzero highest-weight vector \(v\) with \(xv=0\) and
\(hv=\lambda v\). Let \(U_{\mathbb Z}\) be the integer subalgebra of
the universal enveloping algebra generated by all divided powers
\(X_r=x^r/r!\), \(Y_r=y^r/r!\), for integers \(r\geq0\).
An **admissible lattice** \(M\subset V(\lambda)\) is a free abelian
subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis, stable under
\(U_{\mathbb Z}\). It is arbitrary, not necessarily the minimal lattice.

Put \(V(K)=M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\). The Lie algebra
\(L(K)=(\mathbb Zx+\mathbb Zy+\mathbb Zh)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\)
acts by the induced lattice operators. This is the Chevalley
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) construction also in characteristic 2.
Prove that \(V(K)\) is nonzero and every \(K\)-linear subspace
invariant under \(x,y,h\) is zero or all of \(V(K)\).
Both \(\lambda=0\) and \(p=2\) are included; \(K\) need not be
algebraically closed.
value.conclusion: V_K is nonzero, and for every K-linear subspace W of V_K invariant under the induced x,y,h operators, W={0} or W=V_K. Thus V_K is irreducible as a module for the stipulated Chevalley Lie algebra L_K.

parameters.type: Z-submodule of the underlying additive group of V

hypotheses.statement: 0≤lambda<p, with lambda and p compared in Z.
V is the complex irreducible highest-weight sl2(C)-module of highest weight lambda, with the given action x,y,h, and dim_C V=lambda+1.
hx−xh=2x, hy−yh=−2y, and xy−yx=h as complex-linear endomorphisms of V; products mean composition, rightmost first.
M is an arbitrary admissible lattice in V: it has a Z-basis whose images under inclusion form a complex basis of V, and it is stable under U_Z. No minimal-lattice condition is imposed.

definitions.definition: ell=max(lambda,0), viewed as a natural number (Int.toNat lambda).
n=ell+1. Index sets below are I_n={0,...,ell}, equivalently Fin n. In scalar expressions ell−2i is integer subtraction.
For every natural r, X(r)=X_r=(r!:C)^(-1) x^r. Here 0!=1 and the zeroth operator power is Id_V.
For every natural r, Y(r)=Y_r=(r!:C)^(-1) y^r.

definitions.type: integer subalgebra of U(sl2(C)) acting on V
definitions.definition: U_Z is exactly the integer subalgebra of the universal enveloping algebra generated by every divided power x^r/r! and y^r/r! for natural r; its represented generators on V are X_r,Y_r.
V_K=V(K)=M⊗_Z K, with K-scalar action on the second tensor factor. Tensor products are algebraic, generated additively by pure tensors subject to additivity and Z-balancing.
U=K⊗_Z M, with K-scalar action on the first tensor factor.

definitions.type: predicate on a subspace and an endomorphism over a field
definitions.definition: For any field k0, k0-vector space U0, subspace W0 and k0-linear endomorphism f0, Stable(W0,f0) means for every w0∈W0 one has f0(w0)∈W0. Invariance is this predicate.
For i∈Fin(n), e_i=(i!:C)^(-1)y^i v. This formula defines vectors without yet claiming independence.
X_M(r)=X_r^M is the restriction of X_r to M; admissibility supplies its preservation of M.
Y_M(r)=Y_r^M is the restriction of Y_r to M.
x_M=X_M(1), the restriction of x.
y_M=Y_M(1), the restriction of y.
h_M=x_M y_M−y_M x_M. Its identification with the restriction of h is proved internally.
c_j=choose(ell,j), the natural binomial coefficient.
Q_M=Y_M(ell) X_M(ell).
A_ij=X_M(ell−i) Q_M Y_M(ell−j), for indices i,j∈Fin(n); the displayed subtractions are natural and nonnegative.
Dprod=∏_{j∈Fin(n)} c_j.
d_j=∏_{k∈Fin(n), k≠j} c_k; an empty product is 1.

For f∈End_Z(M), define the K-linear operator F(f) by F(f)(a⊗m)=a⊗f(m). The rule is additive and Z-balanced in a,m, so the tensor universal property defines an additive operator, and multiplication on the first factor makes it K-linear. This defines a function, with its ring-homomorphism laws to be proved separately.
S(m⊗a)=a⊗m, extended additively by the tensor universal property: the displayed rule is additive in each input and Z-balanced. K-linearity and bijectivity are proved internally.
S_inv(a⊗m)=m⊗a, defined by the same additive Z-balanced universal property.
red(t) is the image of the integer t in K; for natural t use its integer image first. A bar over an integer or natural denotes red. It preserves finite sums, products and 1.
T_ij=red(c_j)^(-1)·F(A_ij). Field inverse is the usual total inverse (0^(-1)=0); nonvanishing needed for cancellation is proved internally.
ind(f) is the induced lattice operator on V_K, given by ind(f)(m⊗a)=f(m)⊗a. The additive Z-balanced rule defines the operator and is K-linear by the scalar action on the second factor.

L_Z is the free abelian group on the three abstract Chevalley generators, denoted x,y,h in the original problem, with Z-bilinear alternating bracket [h,x]=2x, [h,y]=−2y, [x,y]=h. In formulas for the action, the parameter endomorphisms x,y,h are the respective images of these generators; the integral Lie algebra is not defined as their possibly nonfaithful image in End_C(V).

L_K=L(K)=L_Z⊗_Z K=(Zx+Zy+Zh)⊗_Z K in the original Chevalley notation, with the bracket extended K-bilinearly from the integral bracket. The action on V_K assigns the formal generators the operators ind(x_M),ind(y_M),ind(h_M) and extends K-linearly. Its bracket-preserving property is proved separately. This definition includes characteristic 2.

value.text: H003 gives lambda≥0, hence lambda=(ell:Z) by the definition of Int.toNat, and ell<p. Thus n=ell+1 and H004 gives dim_C V=n. H006 becomes v≠0, xv=0, hv=ell·v. No property of reduction into K is used here.

H005 gives hy=yh−2y and xy=yx+h. Prove h y^i v=(ell−2i)y^i v for every i≥0 by induction: the base is F001; for the step fix t and temporarily assume L1: h y^t v=(ell−2t)y^t v. Then h y^(t+1)v=(yh−2y)y^t v=(ell−2t−2)y^(t+1)v. Discharge L1 to the induction step. For the second identity the base is xyv=yxv+hv=ell v. In the step t≥1, assume L2: xy^t v=t(ell−t+1)y^(t−1)v. Then xy^(t+1)v=y(xy^t v)+hy^t v=[t(ell−t+1)+(ell−2t)]y^t v=(t+1)(ell−t)y^t v. Discharge L2; induction gives xy^i v=i(ell−i+1)y^(i−1)v for every i≥1. These identities do not assume termination.

For each 0≤i≤ell, repeated use of F002 gives x^i y^i v=[∏_{r=1}^i r(ell−r+1)]v. For i>0 all displayed factors are positive integers; for i=0 the product is 1. In C they are nonzero, so v≠0 forces y^i v≠0. Since i!≠0, e_i≠0. F002 also gives he_i=(ell−2i)e_i. The eigenvalues are pairwise distinct: ell−2i=ell−2j in C implies 2(i−j)=0 and hence i=j in characteristic zero.

Take arbitrary coefficients zeta and temporarily assume L3: ∑_i zeta_i e_i=0. Fix j∈Fin(n) and apply ∏_{k≠j}(h−(ell−2k)Id). The factors commute because each is a polynomial in h. Every term of index i≠j is killed by its factor k=i; the surviving term is zeta_j[∏_{k≠j}((ell−2j)−(ell−2k))]e_j=0. By F003 the product and e_j are nonzero, including the empty product. Thus zeta_j=0. This holds for every j. Discharging L3 proves complex linear independence of e.

Apply M001 with division ring C, vector space V, index set Fin(n), and family e. Fin(n) has n elements, V is finite-dimensional of dimension n by F001, and F004 supplies independence. The span is V. Together with independence this makes e a basis.

Put zvec=y^(ell+1)v and alpha_i its e-basis coordinates. M006 with this basis expands zvec=∑_i alpha_i e_i. F002 gives h zvec=(−ell−2)zvec, and applying h−(−ell−2)Id to this expansion gives ∑_i alpha_i[2(ell+1−i)]e_i=0. For every i≤ell the bracketed integer is positive, hence nonzero in C. Independence F004 forces every alpha_i=0, so zvec=0. Applying further powers of y gives y^s v=0 for all s≥ell+1.

Divide the recurrences F002 by i!, using (i+1)!=(i+1)i!, and combine F006 at the top endpoint. This gives xe_0=0, xe_i=(ell−i+1)e_(i−1) for i≥1, ye_i=(i+1)e_(i+1) for i<ell, ye_ell=0 and he_i=(ell−2i)e_i. For r≤i, iteration of x yields ∏_{s=1}^r(ell−i+s) on e_(i−r). After division by r!, M004 at (n0,j0)=(ell−i+r,r), and cancellation of (ell−i)!≠0 in C, gives choose(ell−i+r,r). If r>i the string reaches e_0 and is killed. For i+r≤ell, iteration of y yields (i+r)!/i! on e_(i+r); division by r!, using M004 at (i+r,r), gives choose(i+r,r). If i+r>ell the string reaches e_ell and is killed by y. Thus both zero cases and r=0 are included. These formulas together with F001,F005,F006 prove the full coordinate and termination statement.

By H007 every X_r,Y_r preserves M, so its restriction is a Z-linear endomorphism. Inclusion M→V is injective because M is a submodule. The original complex identities r!X_r=x^r and r!Y_r=y^r therefore restrict to r!X_M(r)=x_M^r and r!Y_M(r)=y_M^r for every r≥0. These are identities using integer multiples of operators, with no division in M. By H005, h=xy−yx, so h preserves M and restricts to h_M=x_M y_M−y_M x_M. The inclusions intertwine x_M,y_M,h_M with x,y,h.

N001 supplies the complex basis e. Define its coordinate endomorphisms E_ij by E_ij e_k=delta_(j,k)e_i. They exist by linear extension on a basis. To record how operator equalities will be checked, fix arbitrary complex endomorphisms fop,gop and temporarily assume L1 that they agree on each e_i. M007, with scalar homomorphism Id_C, yields fop=gop. Discharging L1 and quantifying these maps gives: any two complex-linear endomorphisms agreeing on every e_i are equal.

Put Q_C=Y_ell X_ell. The N001 divided-power formulas show X_ell kills e_k for k<ell and sends e_ell to e_0, while Y_ell e_0=e_ell. Thus Q_C=E_(ell,ell), by F002. They also give X_(ell−i)e_ell=e_i (its binomial coefficient is choose(ell−i,ell−i)=1), so X_(ell−i)Q_C=E_(i,ell) for every i. All formulas include ell=0.

Put A_C_ij=X_(ell−i)Q_C Y_(ell−j). On e_k, if k<j the vector Y_(ell−j)e_k has index below ell and is killed by Q_C; if k>j it goes past the top index and is already zero. For k=j it is choose(ell,ell−j)e_ell. M004 at (ell,j) and (ell,ell−j) gives choose(ell,j) j!(ell−j)!=ell!=choose(ell,ell−j)(ell−j)!j!. Cancel the nonzero integer factorial product to obtain choose(ell,ell−j)=choose(ell,j)=c_j. Hence Q_C Y_(ell−j)=c_j E_(ell,j), and F003 gives A_C_ij=c_j E_ij. In each instance equality on every basis vector is promoted to equality of endomorphisms by F002.

On every basis vector, E_ij E_kl equals E_il if j=k and 0 otherwise; F002 proves the operator identity. By F004, A_C_ij A_C_kl=c_j A_C_il if j=k (both sides are c_j c_l E_il), and 0 otherwise. By definition d_j c_j=Dprod, also for the singleton index set. Acting on e_k gives (∑_j d_j A_C_jj)e_k=Dprod e_k. F002 therefore gives ∑_j d_j A_C_jj=Dprod Id_V.

The products defining Q_M,A_ij are restrictions of Q_C,A_C_ij, since all their divided-power factors preserve M. Thus all coefficients and operators in F005 preserve M, and composition with the injective inclusion M→V transfers each identity to End_Z(M): A_ij A_kl=c_j A_il for j=k and 0 otherwise, and ∑_j d_j A_jj=Dprod Id_M. Along with d_j c_j=Dprod and F001 this proves the full integral-operator statement. Only c_j E_ij is asserted to preserve M over Z.

H003 gives lambda=(ell:Z), so H004 gives dim_C V=n=ell+1. Choose the common integer/complex basis bZ,bC indexed by I from H007. Apply M008 over C to bC: C is nontrivial, and finite-dimensional V is finitely generated, so I is finite. Apply M009 to the same basis: |I|=dim_C V=n. Thus this arbitrary original basis can be reindexed by Fin(n); no specially scaled highest-weight basis of M is assumed.

Choose beta:Fin(n)→I using F001 and let mBasis be the reindexed Z-basis of M. Its images are still a complex basis. Use the canonical baseChange(K) basis qBasis. For arbitrary idx∈Fin(n), M002 identifies qBasis_idx=1⊗mBasis_idx in U=K⊗_Z M. The structure conditions hold because Z is a commutative ring, K has its integer algebra structure, and M is a Z-module. M005 gives dim_K U=|Fin(n)|=n. Here fields have the strong rank condition, the usual invariant-basis-number consequence of linear independence. Since n=ell+1>0, the index 0 exists. qBasis_0≠0: its own basis coordinate at 0 is 1≠0 in K. Thus U≠0.

The K,M,F names in E001's verbatim source statement are source-bound (their ledger aliases are k0,M0,G0). Apply E001 with its source field/module instantiated by the problem K,M, giving a unital ring homomorphism G with G(f)(a⊗m)=a⊗f(m). This is the same pure-tensor formula as D020 F. For each f, both G(f) and F(f) are additive maps, and every tensor is a finite sum of pure tensors, so they agree everywhere. Thus F=G as functions and F itself preserves 1, multiplication, 0 and addition. In particular finite sums, powers, negative operators and integer multiples are preserved. This identifies the prepared adapter with the actual operators used here.

The formulas defining S,S_inv are additive in each input and Z-balanced: for an integer t, the tensor relation a⊗(t m)=(t a)⊗m verifies that moving t between the inputs gives the same value, and the reversed tensor relation verifies this for S_inv. Thus the additive tensor maps are well-defined. For any b,a∈K and m∈M, S(b·(m⊗a))=S(m⊗ba)=ba⊗m=b·S(m⊗a); the same calculation proves K-linearity of S_inv. Their composites fix every pure tensor and hence every finite sum of pure tensors. They are therefore mutual inverses. From F002, U≠0; the isomorphism S then gives V_K≠0.

Fix f0 and a pure tensor m0⊗a0. By the defining formulas, S(ind(f0)(m0⊗a0))=S(f0(m0)⊗a0)=a0⊗f0(m0)=F(f0)(S(m0⊗a0)). Equality extends to every tensor by additivity. Thus S ind(f0)=F(f0) S for every f0. If a subspace is invariant under ind(f0), its image under S is invariant under F(f0); conversely use S_inv. The inverse identities also send zero and whole spaces to zero and whole spaces. With F002,F003,F004 this proves the full scalar-extension, dimension and intertwining statement.

H003 gives lambda=(ell:Z) and ell<p. Since p is prime and char K=p (H001,H002), M003 at r0=ell gives that red(ell!) is a unit, hence nonzero in the field K. For j∈Fin(n), M004 at (ell,j) gives c_j j!(ell−j)!=ell!. After applying red this is red(c_j) red(j!) red((ell−j)!)=red(ell!)≠0. No factor of a nonzero product in a field can be zero, so red(c_j)≠0 for every j. The finite product red(Dprod)=∏_j red(c_j) is nonzero.

Use the ring-homomorphism laws of F from N003 on N002. Integer multiples of an endomorphism become scalar multiples by their image in K: repeated addition and negation commute with F. Scalars commute with K-linear maps. When j≠k, the integer multiplication identity gives T_ij T_k,lidx=0. When j=k it gives T_ij T_j,lidx=red(c_j)^(-1)red(c_lidx)^(-1)F(c_j A_i,lidx)=red(c_lidx)^(-1)F(A_i,lidx)=T_i,lidx. Cancellation uses F001. The sum identity becomes ∑_j red(d_j)F(A_jj)=red(Dprod)Id_U. From d_j c_j=Dprod and F001, red(d_j)=red(Dprod)red(c_j)^(-1); divide the sum identity by the nonzero red(Dprod) to get ∑_j T_jj=Id_U. These are endomorphism identities on U; no reduction of the characteristic-zero e-basis has been presumed.

Fix arbitrary r and temporarily assume L1: r≤ell. Then r<p. M003 gives red(r!) a unit, hence nonzero. N002 gives r! X_M(r)=x_M^r and r! Y_M(r)=y_M^r; N003 lets us apply F, preserving powers and integer multiples. Therefore F(X_M(r))=red(r!)^(-1)F(x_M)^r and F(Y_M(r))=red(r!)^(-1)F(y_M)^r. Discharge L1 and quantify r. The proof only inverts factorials with indices at most ell<p.

Let W be any K-linear subspace of U and temporarily assume L2: W is invariant under F(x_M),F(y_M). By induction it is invariant under every power of each operator, with the identity as the base. Linearity of W and F003 give invariance under F(X_M(r)),F(Y_M(r)) for all r≤ell. The factors in A_ij=X_M(ell−i)Y_M(ell)X_M(ell)Y_M(ell−j) all have indices between 0 and ell, so their F-images preserve W by composition and the ring-homomorphism laws. Finally multiplication by red(c_j)^(-1) preserves W because W is K-linear. Thus every T_ij preserves W. Discharge L2 and universally quantify W. Along with F001,F002 this proves the full reduced matrix-unit and stability statement; Lie invariance has never been used to infer stability of divided powers of index at or above p.

Fix arbitrary k0,n0,U0,T0,W0. Temporarily assume L1: n0>0, dim_{k0} U0=n0, for all i,j,k,l∈Fin(n0), T0_ij T0_kl=T0_il if j=k and 0 otherwise, ∑_j T0_jj=Id_{U0}, and W0 is invariant under all T0_ij. These are precisely the antecedent data of the asserted theorem.

Use the exhaustive cases W0={0} or W0≠{0}. In the zero case L3: W0={0}, the required disjunction follows immediately; discharge L3 for that branch. In the remaining branch assume L2: W0≠{0}. By the definition of a zero subspace there exists a vector in W0 different from 0.
Choose w0∈W0 nonzero using F001. Apply the diagonal-sum identity in L1: w0=∑_j T0_jj(w0). If every summand were zero, w0 would be zero. Hence there exists j∈Fin(n0) with T0_jj(w0)≠0.

Choose j0 from F002 and put u0=T0_j0,j0(w0). Stability gives u0∈W0; it is nonzero by choice. The relation T0_j0,j0^2=T0_j0,j0 gives T0_j0,j0(u0)=u0. Define uFamily_i=T0_i,j0(u0). Every uFamily_i belongs to W0 by stability.

Take arbitrary coefficients acoef and assume L4: ∑_i acoef_i uFamily_i=0. Fix kidx∈Fin(n0) and apply T0_j0,kidx. The multiplication law from L1 kills every term except i=kidx, yielding 0=∑_i acoef_i T0_j0,kidx T0_i,j0(u0)=acoef_kidx T0_j0,j0(u0)=acoef_kidx u0. Since k0 is a field and u0≠0 by F003, acoef_kidx=0. This holds for every kidx. Discharge L4 to prove linear independence of uFamily.

Apply M001 to the field k0 (a division ring), the finite-dimensional U0, Fin(n0), and uFamily. L1 gives dim U0=n0 and F004 gives independence, so this family's span is U0. F003 says every family vector is in W0, so closure under linear combinations gives W0=U0 in the nonzero branch. Discharge L2 and combine it with the zero branch of S002, obtaining W0={0} or W0=U0. Discharge L1 to the full implication, and universally quantify all the originally arbitrary data. This proves the asserted general irreducibility lemma, even if n0 has zero image in k0: there was no division by n0 or trace calculation.

H007 and N002 identify x_M,y_M,h_M with the integral restrictions of the stipulated x,y,h. Their integer Chevalley relations follow from H005 by applying the injective inclusion M→V: [h_M,x_M]=2x_M, [h_M,y_M]=−2y_M and [x_M,y_M]=h_M. By N003, scalar extension F preserves these identities, and S intertwines F with each induced operator ind on V_K. Thus the original induced x,y,h actions are exactly ind(x_M),ind(y_M),ind(h_M), with the stipulated Chevalley relations after tensoring over Z. This is valid in characteristic 2 as well: the L_K=L_Z⊗_Z K action is the K-linear extension of the integral action of the three formal Chevalley generators. Invariance under the three generators is equivalent to invariance under every K-linear combination of them. N003 already gives V_K≠0.

Let W be any K-linear subspace of V_K, and assume L1: W is invariant under the induced x,y,h operators. Put Zsub=S(W). By N003 it is a K-linear subspace of U; the intertwining formulas and L1 make it invariant under F(x_M),F(y_M). N004 therefore makes it invariant under all T_ij and supplies the multiplication and diagonal-sum relations. N003 gives dim_K U=n=ell+1>0. Apply N005 at field K, size n, space U, family T and subspace Zsub: Zsub={0} or Zsub=U. Apply S_inv, using the inverse identities in N003, to obtain W={0} or W=V_K. Discharge L1 and quantify W. Together with nonzeroness from N003 this proves P.

For the endpoints, H003 gives ell<p, H001 gives p prime, and H002 gives char K=p. If lambda=0 then ell=0,n=1, X_0=Y_0=Id, c_0=Dprod=d_0=1, and all the same formulas apply. If p=2 then ell∈{0,1}; every factorial inverted in the stability argument has index at most ell<2. The e-basis in N001 lives in V over C; none of the reduced matrix-unit premises used in S002 requires distinct h-eigenvalues in K. No step imposed algebraic closure of K or a minimal-lattice condition. Thus the conclusion covers the complete original parameter range.

import Mathlib

namespace YuiBasisObjects

noncomputable def dividedPower {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (f : Module.End ℂ V) (r : ℕ) : Module.End ℂ V :=
  ((r.factorial : ℂ)⁻¹) • f ^ r

def Stable {K V : Type*} [Field K] [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V]
    (W : Submodule K V) (f : Module.End K V) : Prop :=
  ∀ w, w ∈ W → f w ∈ W

structure AdmissibleLattice (n : ℕ) (V : Type*) [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (x y : Module.End ℂ V) where
  carrier : Submodule ℤ V
  zBasis : Module.Basis (Fin n) ℤ carrier
  cBasis : Module.Basis (Fin n) ℂ V
  coe_basis : ∀ i, (zBasis i : V) = cBasis i
  stableX : ∀ (r : ℕ) (m : V), m ∈ carrier → dividedPower x r m ∈ carrier
  stableY : ∀ (r : ℕ) (m : V), m ∈ carrier → dividedPower y r m ∈ carrier

Let \(p\) be any prime, \(K\) any field of characteristic \(p\), and
\(\lambda\) an integer with \(0\leq\lambda<p\).
Let \(V(\lambda)\) be the complex irreducible highest-weight
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\)-module of highest weight \(\lambda\),
of dimension \(\lambda+1\). Its Chevalley generators satisfy

\[
[h,x]=2x,\qquad[h,y]=-2y,\qquad[x,y]=h.
\]

Choose a nonzero highest-weight vector \(v\) with \(xv=0\) and
\(hv=\lambda v\). Let \(U_{\mathbb Z}\) be the integer subalgebra of
the universal enveloping algebra generated by all divided powers
\(X_r=x^r/r!\), \(Y_r=y^r/r!\), for integers \(r\geq0\).
An **admissible lattice** \(M\subset V(\lambda)\) is a free abelian
subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis, stable under
\(U_{\mathbb Z}\). It is arbitrary, not necessarily the minimal lattice.

Put \(V(K)=M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\). The Lie algebra
\(L(K)=(\mathbb Zx+\mathbb Zy+\mathbb Zh)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\)
acts by the induced lattice operators. This is the Chevalley
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) construction also in characteristic 2.
Prove that \(V(K)\) is nonzero and every \(K\)-linear subspace
invariant under \(x,y,h\) is zero or all of \(V(K)\).
Both \(\lambda=0\) and \(p=2\) are included; \(K\) need not be
algebraically closed.

Transfer any invariant subspace through the intertwining tensor swap B104, apply B103 and B105, and transfer back. B104 supplies nonzeroness. The p=2 and lambda=0 cases are covered by the same formulas.

import Mathlib

namespace YuiBasisObjects

noncomputable def dividedPower {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (f : Module.End ℂ V) (r : ℕ) : Module.End ℂ V :=
  ((r.factorial : ℂ)⁻¹) • f ^ r

def Stable {K V : Type*} [Field K] [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V]
    (W : Submodule K V) (f : Module.End K V) : Prop :=
  ∀ w, w ∈ W → f w ∈ W

structure AdmissibleLattice (n : ℕ) (V : Type*) [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (x y : Module.End ℂ V) where
  carrier : Submodule ℤ V
  zBasis : Module.Basis (Fin n) ℤ carrier
  cBasis : Module.Basis (Fin n) ℂ V
  coe_basis : ∀ i, (zBasis i : V) = cBasis i
  stableX : ∀ (r : ℕ) (m : V), m ∈ carrier → dividedPower x r m ∈ carrier
  stableY : ∀ (r : ℕ) (m : V), m ∈ carrier → dividedPower y r m ∈ carrier

end YuiBasisObjects

value.statement:
Let \(p\) be any prime, \(K\) any field of characteristic \(p\), and
\(\lambda\) an integer with \(0\leq\lambda<p\).
Let \(V(\lambda)\) be the complex irreducible highest-weight
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\)-module of highest weight \(\lambda\),
of dimension \(\lambda+1\). Its Chevalley generators satisfy

\[
[h,x]=2x,\qquad[h,y]=-2y,\qquad[x,y]=h.
\]

Choose a nonzero highest-weight vector \(v\) with \(xv=0\) and
\(hv=\lambda v\). Let \(U_{\mathbb Z}\) be the integer subalgebra of
the universal enveloping algebra generated by all divided powers
\(X_r=x^r/r!\), \(Y_r=y^r/r!\), for integers \(r\geq0\).
An **admissible lattice** \(M\subset V(\lambda)\) is a free abelian
subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis, stable under
\(U_{\mathbb Z}\). It is arbitrary, not necessarily the minimal lattice.

Put \(V(K)=M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\). The Lie algebra
\(L(K)=(\mathbb Zx+\mathbb Zy+\mathbb Zh)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\)
acts by the induced lattice operators. This is the Chevalley
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) construction also in characteristic 2.
Prove that \(V(K)\) is nonzero and every \(K\)-linear subspace
invariant under \(x,y,h\) is zero or all of \(V(K)\).
Both \(\lambda=0\) and \(p=2\) are included; \(K\) need not be
algebraically closed.

Transfer any invariant subspace through the intertwining tensor swap B104, apply B103 and B105, and transfer back. B104 supplies nonzeroness. The p=2 and lambda=0 cases are covered by the same formulas.

641: open TensorProduct

643: /-!
644: ### The base-change of a linear map of `R`-modules to a linear map of `A`-modules
645: -/
646: 
647: 
648: section Semiring
649: 
650: variable {R A B M N P : Type*} [CommSemiring R]
651: variable [Semiring A] [Algebra R A] [Semiring B] [Algebra R B]
652: variable [AddCommMonoid M] [AddCommMonoid N] [AddCommMonoid P]
653: variable [Module R M] [Module R N] [Module R P]
654: variable (r : R) (f g : M →ₗ[R] N)
655: 
656: variable (A) in
657: /-- `baseChange A f` for `f : M →ₗ[R] N` is the `A`-linear map `A ⊗[R] M →ₗ[A] A ⊗[R] N`.
658: 
659: This "base change" operation is also known as "extension of scalars". -/
660: def baseChange (f : M →ₗ[R] N) : A ⊗[R] M →ₗ[A] A ⊗[R] N :=
661:   AlgebraTensorModule.map (LinearMap.id : A →ₗ[A] A) f
662: 
663: @[simp]
664: theorem baseChange_tmul (a : A) (x : M) : f.baseChange A (a ⊗ₜ x) = a ⊗ₜ f x :=
665:   rfl
666: 
667: theorem baseChange_eq_ltensor : (f.baseChange A : A ⊗ M → A ⊗ N) = f.lTensor A :=
668:   rfl
669: 
670: @[simp]
671: theorem baseChange_add : (f + g).baseChange A = f.baseChange A + g.baseChange A := by
672:   ext
673:   simp [baseChange_eq_ltensor, -baseChange_tmul]
674: 
675: @[simp]
676: theorem baseChange_zero : baseChange A (0 : M →ₗ[R] N) = 0 := by
677:   ext
678:   simp
679: 
680: @[simp]
681: theorem baseChange_smul : (r • f).baseChange A = r • f.baseChange A := by
682:   ext
683:   simp
684: 
685: @[simp]
686: lemma baseChange_id : (.id : M →ₗ[R] M).baseChange A = .id := by
687:   ext; simp
688: 
689: lemma baseChange_comp (g : N →ₗ[R] P) :
690:     (g ∘ₗ f).baseChange A = g.baseChange A ∘ₗ f.baseChange A := by
691:   ext; simp
692: 
693: open AlgebraTensorModule in
694: lemma baseChange_baseChange {A B : Type*} [CommSemiring A] [Algebra R A]
695:     [Semiring B] [Algebra R B] [Algebra A B] [IsScalarTower R A B]
696:     (f : M →ₗ[R] N) :
697:     ((f.baseChange A).baseChange B) =
698:     (cancelBaseChange R A B B N).symm ∘ₗ
699:       (f.baseChange B) ∘ₗ (cancelBaseChange R A B B M) := by
700:   ext; simp
701: 
702: variable (R M) in
703: @[simp]
704: lemma baseChange_one : (1 : Module.End R M).baseChange A = 1 := baseChange_id
705: 
706: lemma baseChange_mul (f g : Module.End R M) :
707:     (f * g).baseChange A = f.baseChange A * g.baseChange A := by
708:   ext; simp
709:

64: /-- The relation on `FreeAddMonoid (M × N)` that generates a congruence whose quotient is
65: the tensor product. -/
66: inductive Eqv : FreeAddMonoid (M × N) → FreeAddMonoid (M × N) → Prop
67:   | of_zero_left : ∀ n : N, Eqv (.of (0, n)) 0
68:   | of_zero_right : ∀ m : M, Eqv (.of (m, 0)) 0
69:   | of_add_left : ∀ (m₁ m₂ : M) (n : N), Eqv (.of (m₁, n) + .of (m₂, n)) (.of (m₁ + m₂, n))
70:   | of_add_right : ∀ (m : M) (n₁ n₂ : N), Eqv (.of (m, n₁) + .of (m, n₂)) (.of (m, n₁ + n₂))
71:   | of_smul : ∀ (r : R) (m : M) (n : N), Eqv (.of (r • m, n)) (.of (m, r • n))
72:   | add_comm : ∀ x y, Eqv (x + y) (y + x)
73: 
74: end

168: /-- A typeclass for `SMul` structures which can be moved across a tensor product.
169: 
170: This typeclass is generated automatically from an `IsScalarTower` instance, but exists so that
171: we can also add an instance for `AddCommGroup.toIntModule`, allowing `z •` to be moved even if
172: `R` does not support negation.
173: 
174: Note that `Module R' (M ⊗[R] N)` is available even without this typeclass on `R'`; it's only
175: needed if `TensorProduct.smul_tmul`, `TensorProduct.smul_tmul'`, or `TensorProduct.tmul_smul` is
176: used.
177: -/
178: class CompatibleSMul [DistribMulAction R' N] : Prop where
179:   smul_tmul : ∀ (r : R') (m : M) (n : N), (r • m) ⊗ₜ n = m ⊗ₜ[R] (r • n)
180: 
181: end
182: 
183: /-- Note that this provides the default `CompatibleSMul R R M N` instance through
184: `IsScalarTower.left`. -/
185: instance (priority := 100) CompatibleSMul.isScalarTower [SMul R' R] [IsScalarTower R' R M]
186:     [DistribMulAction R' N] [IsScalarTower R' R N] : CompatibleSMul R R' M N :=
187:   ⟨fun r m n => by
188:     conv_lhs => rw [← one_smul R m]
189:     conv_rhs => rw [← one_smul R n]
190:     rw [← smul_assoc, ← smul_assoc]
191:     exact Quotient.sound' <| AddConGen.Rel.of _ _ <| Eqv.of_smul _ _ _⟩
192: 
193: /-- `smul` can be moved from one side of the product to the other . -/
194: theorem smul_tmul [DistribMulAction R' N] [CompatibleSMul R R' M N] (r : R') (m : M) (n : N) :
195:     (r • m) ⊗ₜ n = m ⊗ₜ[R] (r • n) :=
196:   CompatibleSMul.smul_tmul _ _ _
197: 
198: set_option backward.privateInPublic true in
199: @[instance_reducible]
200: private def addMonoidWithWrongNSMul : AddMonoid (M ⊗[R] N) :=
201:   { (addConGen (TensorProduct.Eqv R M N)).addMonoid with }
202: 
203: attribute [local instance] addMonoidWithWrongNSMul in
204: /-- Auxiliary function to defining scalar multiplication on tensor product. -/
205: def SMul.aux {R' : Type*} [SMul R' M] (r : R') : FreeAddMonoid (M × N) →+ M ⊗[R] N :=
206:   FreeAddMonoid.lift fun p : M × N => (r • p.1) ⊗ₜ p.2
207: 
208: theorem SMul.aux_of {R' : Type*} [SMul R' M] (r : R') (m : M) (n : N) :
209:     SMul.aux r (.of (m, n)) = (r • m) ⊗ₜ[R] n :=
210:   rfl
211: 
212: variable [SMulCommClass R R' M] [SMulCommClass R R'' M]
213: 
214: /-- Given two modules over a commutative semiring `R`, if one of the factors carries a
215: (distributive) action of a second type of scalars `R'`, which commutes with the action of `R`, then
216: the tensor product (over `R`) carries an action of `R'`.
217: 
218: This instance defines this `R'` action in the case that it is the left module which has the `R'`
219: action. Two natural ways in which this situation arises are:
220: * Extension of scalars
221: * A tensor product of a group representation with a module not carrying an action
222: 
223: Note that in the special case that `R = R'`, since `R` is commutative, we just get the usual scalar
224: action on a tensor product of two modules. This special case is important enough that, for
225: performance reasons, we define it explicitly below. -/
226: instance leftHasSMul : SMul R' (M ⊗[R] N) :=
227:   id ⟨fun r =>
228:     (addConGen (TensorProduct.Eqv R M N)).lift (SMul.aux r : _ →+ M ⊗[R] N) <|
229:       AddCon.addConGen_le.2 fun x y hxy =>
230:         match x, y, hxy with
231:         | _, _, .of_zero_left n =>
232:           (AddCon.ker_rel _).2 <| by simp_rw [map_zero, SMul.aux_of, smul_zero, zero_tmul]
233:         | _, _, .of_zero_right m =>
234:           (AddCon.ker_rel _).2 <| by simp_rw [map_zero, SMul.aux_of, tmul_zero]
235:         | _, _, .of_add_left m₁ m₂ n =>
236:           (AddCon.ker_rel _).2 <| by simp_rw [map_add, SMul.aux_of, smul_add, add_tmul]
237:         | _, _, .of_add_right m n₁ n₂ =>
238:           (AddCon.ker_rel _).2 <| by simp_rw [map_add, SMul.aux_of, tmul_add]
239:         | _, _, .of_smul s m n =>
240:           (AddCon.ker_rel _).2 <| by rw [SMul.aux_of, SMul.aux_of, ← smul_comm, smul_tmul]
241:         | _, _, .add_comm x y =>
242:           (AddCon.ker_rel _).2 <| by simp_rw [map_add, add_comm]⟩
243: 
244: instance : SMul R (M ⊗[R] N) :=
245:   TensorProduct.leftHasSMul
246: 
247: protected theorem smul_zero (r : R') : r • (0 : M ⊗[R] N) = 0 :=
248:   map_zero _
249: 
250: protected theorem smul_add (r : R') (x y : M ⊗[R] N) : r • (x + y) = r • x + r • y :=
251:   map_add _ _ _
252: 
253: protected theorem zero_smul (x : M ⊗[R] N) : (0 : R'') • x = 0 :=
254:   have : ∀ (r : R'') (m : M) (n : N), r • m ⊗ₜ[R] n = (r • m) ⊗ₜ n := fun _ _ _ => rfl
255:   x.induction_on (by rw [TensorProduct.smul_zero])
256:     (fun m n => by rw [this, zero_smul, zero_tmul]) fun x y ihx ihy => by
257:     rw [TensorProduct.smul_add, ihx, ihy, add_zero]
258: 
259: protected theorem one_smul (x : M ⊗[R] N) : (1 : R') • x = x :=
260:   have : ∀ (r : R') (m : M) (n : N), r • m ⊗ₜ[R] n = (r • m) ⊗ₜ n := fun _ _ _ => rfl
261:   x.induction_on (by rw [TensorProduct.smul_zero])
262:     (fun m n => by rw [this, one_smul])
263:     fun x y ihx ihy => by rw [TensorProduct.smul_add, ihx, ihy]
264: 
265: protected theorem add_smul (r s : R'') (x : M ⊗[R] N) : (r + s) • x = r • x + s • x :=
266:   have : ∀ (r : R'') (m : M) (n : N), r • m ⊗ₜ[R] n = (r • m) ⊗ₜ n := fun _ _ _ => rfl
267:   x.induction_on (by simp_rw [TensorProduct.smul_zero, add_zero])
268:     (fun m n => by simp_rw [this, add_smul, add_tmul]) fun x y ihx ihy => by
269:     simp_rw [TensorProduct.smul_add]
270:     rw [ihx, ihy, add_add_add_comm]
271: 
272: instance addMonoid : AddMonoid (M ⊗[R] N) where
273:   nsmul_zero := by simp [TensorProduct.zero_smul]
274:   nsmul_succ := by simp only [TensorProduct.one_smul, TensorProduct.add_smul, forall_const]
275: 
276: instance addCommMonoid : AddCommMonoid (M ⊗[R] N) where
277: 
278: variable (R)
279: 
280: theorem _root_.IsAddUnit.tmul_left {n : N} (hn : IsAddUnit n) (m : M) : IsAddUnit (m ⊗ₜ[R] n) := by
281:   rw [isAddUnit_iff_exists_neg] at hn ⊢
282:   have ⟨b, eq⟩ := hn
283:   exact ⟨m ⊗ₜ[R] b, by rw [← tmul_add, eq, tmul_zero]⟩
284: 
285: theorem _root_.IsAddUnit.tmul_right {m : M} (hm : IsAddUnit m) (n : N) : IsAddUnit (m ⊗ₜ[R] n) := by
286:   rw [isAddUnit_iff_exists_neg] at hm ⊢
287:   have ⟨b, eq⟩ := hm
288:   exact ⟨b ⊗ₜ[R] n, by rw [← add_tmul, eq, zero_tmul]⟩
289: 
290: variable {R}
291: 
292: instance leftDistribMulAction : DistribMulAction R' (M ⊗[R] N) :=
293:   have : ∀ (r : R') (m : M) (n : N), r • m ⊗ₜ[R] n = (r • m) ⊗ₜ n := fun _ _ _ => rfl
294:   { smul_add := fun r x y => TensorProduct.smul_add r x y
295:     mul_smul := fun r s x =>
296:       x.induction_on (by simp_rw [TensorProduct.smul_zero])
297:         (fun m n => by simp_rw [this, mul_smul]) fun x y ihx ihy => by
298:         simp_rw [TensorProduct.smul_add]
299:         rw [ihx, ihy]
300:     one_smul := TensorProduct.one_smul
301:     smul_zero := TensorProduct.smul_zero }
302: 
303: instance : DistribMulAction R (M ⊗[R] N) :=
304:   TensorProduct.leftDistribMulAction
305: 
306: theorem smul_tmul' (r : R') (m : M) (n : N) : r • m ⊗ₜ[R] n = (r • m) ⊗ₜ n :=
307:   rfl
308: 
309: @[simp]
310: theorem tmul_smul [DistribMulAction R' N] [CompatibleSMul R R' M N] (r : R') (x : M) (y : N) :
311:     x ⊗ₜ (r • y) = r • x ⊗ₜ[R] y :=
312:   (smul_tmul _ _ _).symm

variable {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
noncomputable def e (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (i : ℕ) : V :=
  (i.factorial : ℂ)⁻¹ • (y ^ i) v
def c (ell : ℕ) (j : Fin (ell + 1)) : ℕ := Nat.choose ell j.val
def Dprod (ell : ℕ) : ℕ := ∏ j : Fin (ell + 1), c ell j
def d (ell : ℕ) (j : Fin (ell + 1)) : ℕ :=
  ∏ k : Fin (ell + 1), if k = j then 1 else c ell k
def hM {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℤ M]
    (XM YM : ℕ → Module.End ℤ M) : Module.End ℤ M :=
  XM 1 * YM 1 - YM 1 * XM 1

  XM (ell - i.val) * (YM ell * XM ell) * YM (ell - j.val)

  TensorProduct ℤ M K

    AddCommGroup (VK K M) := inferInstanceAs (AddCommGroup (TensorProduct ℤ M K))
noncomputable instance vkModule (K M : Type*) [Field K] [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℤ M] :
    Module K (VK K M) := (TensorProduct.comm ℤ M K).toAddEquiv.module K
noncomputable def swap (K M : Type*) [Field K] [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℤ M] :
    VK K M ≃ₗ[K] TensorProduct ℤ K M :=
  (TensorProduct.comm ℤ M K).toAddEquiv.linearEquiv K

    (f : Module.End ℤ M) : Module.End K (TensorProduct ℤ K M) := f.baseChange K

    (f : Module.End ℤ M) : Module.End K (VK K M) :=

noncomputable def T (K : Type*) {M : Type*} [Field K] [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℤ M]
    (XM YM : ℕ → Module.End ℤ M) (ell : ℕ)
    (i j : Fin (ell + 1)) : Module.End K (TensorProduct ℤ K M) :=
  (c ell j : K)⁻¹ • F K (A XM YM ell i j)
def MatrixUnits {k : Type*} [Field k] {U : Type*} [AddCommGroup U] [Module k U]
    (n : ℕ) (t : Fin n → Fin n → Module.End k U) : Prop :=

import Mathlib

namespace YuiBasisObjects

noncomputable def dividedPower {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (f : Module.End ℂ V) (r : ℕ) : Module.End ℂ V :=
  ((r.factorial : ℂ)⁻¹) • f ^ r

def Stable {K V : Type*} [Field K] [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V]
    (W : Submodule K V) (f : Module.End K V) : Prop :=
  ∀ w, w ∈ W → f w ∈ W

structure AdmissibleLattice (n : ℕ) (V : Type*) [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (x y : Module.End ℂ V) where
  carrier : Submodule ℤ V
  zBasis : Module.Basis (Fin n) ℤ carrier
  cBasis : Module.Basis (Fin n) ℂ V
  coe_basis : ∀ i, (zBasis i : V) = cBasis i
  stableX : ∀ (r : ℕ) (m : V), m ∈ carrier → dividedPower x r m ∈ carrier
  stableY : ∀ (r : ℕ) (m : V), m ∈ carrier → dividedPower y r m ∈ carrier

end YuiBasisObjects

namespace Reduction
open scoped BigOperators
open YuiBasisObjects
variable {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
noncomputable def e (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (i : ℕ) : V :=
  (i.factorial : ℂ)⁻¹ • (y ^ i) v
def c (ell : ℕ) (j : Fin (ell + 1)) : ℕ := Nat.choose ell j.val
def Dprod (ell : ℕ) : ℕ := ∏ j : Fin (ell + 1), c ell j
def d (ell : ℕ) (j : Fin (ell + 1)) : ℕ :=
  ∏ k : Fin (ell + 1), if k = j then 1 else c ell k
def hM {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℤ M]
    (XM YM : ℕ → Module.End ℤ M) : Module.End ℤ M :=
  XM 1 * YM 1 - YM 1 * XM 1
def A {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℤ M]
    (XM YM : ℕ → Module.End ℤ M) (ell : ℕ)
    (i j : Fin (ell + 1)) : Module.End ℤ M :=
  XM (ell - i.val) * (YM ell * XM ell) * YM (ell - j.val)
def VK (K M : Type*) [Field K] [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℤ M] :=
  TensorProduct ℤ M K
noncomputable instance vkAdd (K M : Type*) [Field K] [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℤ M] :
    AddCommGroup (VK K M) := inferInstanceAs (AddCommGroup (TensorProduct ℤ M K))
noncomputable def swapAdd (K M : Type*) [Field K] [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℤ M] :
    VK K M ≃+ TensorProduct ℤ K M :=
  let f : TensorProduct ℤ M K ≃ₗ[ℤ] TensorProduct ℤ K M := TensorProduct.comm ℤ M K
  f.toAddEquiv
noncomputable instance vkModule (K M : Type*) [Field K] [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℤ M] :
    Module K (VK K M) := (swapAdd K M).module K
noncomputable def swap (K M : Type*) [Field K] [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℤ M] :
    VK K M ≃ₗ[K] TensorProduct ℤ K M :=
  (swapAdd K M).linearEquiv K
noncomputable def F (K : Type*) {M : Type*} [Field K] [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℤ M]
    (f : Module.End ℤ M) : Module.End K (TensorProduct ℤ K M) := f.baseChange K
noncomputable def ind (K : Type*) {M : Type*} [Field K] [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℤ M]
    (f : Module.End ℤ M) : Module.End K (VK K M) :=
  (swap K M).symm.toLinearMap ∘ₗ F K f ∘ₗ (swap K M).toLinearMap
noncomputable def T (K : Type*) {M : Type*} [Field K] [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℤ M]
    (XM YM : ℕ → Module.End ℤ M) (ell : ℕ)
    (i j : Fin (ell + 1)) : Module.End K (TensorProduct ℤ K M) :=
  (c ell j : K)⁻¹ • F K (A XM YM ell i j)
def MatrixUnits {k : Type*} [Field k] {U : Type*} [AddCommGroup U] [Module k U]
    (n : ℕ) (t : Fin n → Fin n → Module.End k U) : Prop :=
  (∀ i j a b, t i j * t a b = if j = a then t i b else 0) ∧
  (∑ j, t j j) = 1
end Reduction

43:     Module R α :=

import Mathlib

namespace YuiBasisObjects

noncomputable def dividedPower {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (f : Module.End ℂ V) (r : ℕ) : Module.End ℂ V :=
  ((r.factorial : ℂ)⁻¹) • f ^ r

def Stable {K V : Type*} [Field K] [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V]
    (W : Submodule K V) (f : Module.End K V) : Prop :=
  ∀ w, w ∈ W → f w ∈ W

structure AdmissibleLattice (n : ℕ) (V : Type*) [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (x y : Module.End ℂ V) where
  carrier : Submodule ℤ V
  zBasis : Module.Basis (Fin n) ℤ carrier
  cBasis : Module.Basis (Fin n) ℂ V
  coe_basis : ∀ i, (zBasis i : V) = cBasis i
  stableX : ∀ (r : ℕ) (m : V), m ∈ carrier → dividedPower x r m ∈ carrier
  stableY : ∀ (r : ℕ) (m : V), m ∈ carrier → dividedPower y r m ∈ carrier

end YuiBasisObjects

namespace Reduction
open scoped BigOperators
open YuiBasisObjects
variable {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
noncomputable def e (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (i : ℕ) : V :=
  (i.factorial : ℂ)⁻¹ • (y ^ i) v
def c (ell : ℕ) (j : Fin (ell + 1)) : ℕ := Nat.choose ell j.val
def Dprod (ell : ℕ) : ℕ := ∏ j : Fin (ell + 1), c ell j
def d (ell : ℕ) (j : Fin (ell + 1)) : ℕ :=
  ∏ k : Fin (ell + 1), if k = j then 1 else c ell k
def hM {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℤ M]
    (XM YM : ℕ → Module.End ℤ M) : Module.End ℤ M :=
  XM 1 * YM 1 - YM 1 * XM 1
def A {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℤ M]
    (XM YM : ℕ → Module.End ℤ M) (ell : ℕ)
    (i j : Fin (ell + 1)) : Module.End ℤ M :=
  XM (ell - i.val) * (YM ell * XM ell) * YM (ell - j.val)
def VK (K M : Type*) [Field K] [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℤ M] :=
  TensorProduct ℤ M K
noncomputable instance vkAdd (K M : Type*) [Field K] [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℤ M] :
    AddCommGroup (VK K M) := inferInstanceAs (AddCommGroup (TensorProduct ℤ M K))
noncomputable def swapAdd (K M : Type*) [Field K] [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℤ M] :
    VK K M ≃+ TensorProduct ℤ K M :=
  letI : Module ℤ (TensorProduct ℤ M K) := TensorProduct.instModule
  letI : Module ℤ (TensorProduct ℤ K M) := TensorProduct.instModule
  (TensorProduct.comm ℤ M K).toAddEquiv
noncomputable instance vkModule (K M : Type*) [Field K] [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℤ M] :
    Module K (VK K M) := (swapAdd K M).module K
noncomputable def swap (K M : Type*) [Field K] [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℤ M] :
    VK K M ≃ₗ[K] TensorProduct ℤ K M :=
  (swapAdd K M).linearEquiv K
noncomputable def F (K : Type*) {M : Type*} [Field K] [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℤ M]
    (f : Module.End ℤ M) : Module.End K (TensorProduct ℤ K M) := f.baseChange K
noncomputable def ind (K : Type*) {M : Type*} [Field K] [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℤ M]
    (f : Module.End ℤ M) : Module.End K (VK K M) :=
  (swap K M).symm.toLinearMap ∘ₗ F K f ∘ₗ (swap K M).toLinearMap
noncomputable def T (K : Type*) {M : Type*} [Field K] [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℤ M]
    (XM YM : ℕ → Module.End ℤ M) (ell : ℕ)
    (i j : Fin (ell + 1)) : Module.End K (TensorProduct ℤ K M) :=
  (c ell j : K)⁻¹ • F K (A XM YM ell i j)
def MatrixUnits {k : Type*} [Field k] {U : Type*} [AddCommGroup U] [Module k U]
    (n : ℕ) (t : Fin n → Fin n → Module.End k U) : Prop :=
  (∀ i j a b, t i j * t a b = if j = a then t i b else 0) ∧
  (∑ j, t j j) = 1
end Reduction
types: Nonempty (Reduction.VK K M ≃ₗ[K] TensorProduct ℤ K M)
∀ w : Reduction.VK K M, Reduction.swap K M w = Reduction.swap K M w
Reduction.MatrixUnits (lambda.toNat + 1) (Reduction.T K XM YM lambda.toNat)

The lattice is the original integer submodule M, with XM/YM the uniquely determined restrictions, specified in H007. Use both tensor orders with a transported right-factor K-module on VK; prove the pure-tensor and invariant-subspace identifications in N003. No background note is a premise, and all M results are direct library uses.

P.explanation: All original H roots remain. H004 expresses the finite-dimensional irreducible highest-weight representation by its three generator operators, dimension and existence of a highest-weight vector; H005 fixes their Chevalley relations and H006 the chosen vector. H007 states the common integer/complex basis and specifies the unique restricted divided powers XM/YM: original stability supplies these restrictions, and their existence implies stability; closure under the generated integer algebra is equivalent to generator stability. No lattice minimality is imposed. VK is M⊗ℤK with the K-module transported by tensor commutation; T008 proves that this action multiplies the second factor and that ind(f)(m⊗a)=f(m)⊗a, together with the invariant-subspace transport in both directions. Thus Nontrivial VK and the universal zero-or-whole assertion are exactly the full original target. T012 checks the three integral/reduced Chevalley relations, so stability under their K-linear combinations is stability under the stipulated free Chevalley Lie algebra, including characteristic 2. Integers lambda, arbitrary fields of prime characteristic, lambda=0 and p=2 are retained.

import Mathlib

namespace YuiBasisObjects

noncomputable def dividedPower {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (f : Module.End ℂ V) (r : ℕ) : Module.End ℂ V :=
  ((r.factorial : ℂ)⁻¹) • f ^ r

def Stable {K V : Type*} [Field K] [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V]
    (W : Submodule K V) (f : Module.End K V) : Prop :=
  ∀ w, w ∈ W → f w ∈ W

structure AdmissibleLattice (n : ℕ) (V : Type*) [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (x y : Module.End ℂ V) where
  carrier : Submodule ℤ V
  zBasis : Module.Basis (Fin n) ℤ carrier
  cBasis : Module.Basis (Fin n) ℂ V
  coe_basis : ∀ i, (zBasis i : V) = cBasis i
  stableX : ∀ (r : ℕ) (m : V), m ∈ carrier → dividedPower x r m ∈ carrier
  stableY : ∀ (r : ℕ) (m : V), m ∈ carrier → dividedPower y r m ∈ carrier

end YuiBasisObjects

universe uK uV

namespace Reduction
open scoped BigOperators
open YuiBasisObjects
variable {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
noncomputable def e (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (i : ℕ) : V :=
  (i.factorial : ℂ)⁻¹ • (y ^ i) v
def c (ell : ℕ) (j : Fin (ell + 1)) : ℕ := Nat.choose ell j.val
def Dprod (ell : ℕ) : ℕ := ∏ j : Fin (ell + 1), c ell j
def d (ell : ℕ) (j : Fin (ell + 1)) : ℕ :=
  ∏ k : Fin (ell + 1), if k = j then 1 else c ell k
def hM {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℤ M]
    (XM YM : ℕ → Module.End ℤ M) : Module.End ℤ M :=
  XM 1 * YM 1 - YM 1 * XM 1
def A {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℤ M]
    (XM YM : ℕ → Module.End ℤ M) (ell : ℕ)
    (i j : Fin (ell + 1)) : Module.End ℤ M :=
  XM (ell - i.val) * (YM ell * XM ell) * YM (ell - j.val)
noncomputable def AC (x y : Module.End ℂ V) (ell : ℕ)
    (i j : Fin (ell + 1)) : Module.End ℂ V :=
  dividedPower x (ell - i.val) *
    (dividedPower y ell * dividedPower x ell) * dividedPower y (ell - j.val)
def VK (K M : Type*) [Field K] [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℤ M] :=
  TensorProduct ℤ M K
noncomputable instance vkAdd (K M : Type*) [Field K] [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℤ M] :
    AddCommGroup (VK K M) := inferInstanceAs (AddCommGroup (TensorProduct ℤ M K))
noncomputable def swapAdd (K M : Type*) [Field K] [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℤ M] :
    VK K M ≃+ TensorProduct ℤ K M :=
  letI : Module ℤ (TensorProduct ℤ M K) := TensorProduct.instModule
  letI : Module ℤ (TensorProduct ℤ K M) := TensorProduct.instModule
  (TensorProduct.comm ℤ M K).toAddEquiv
noncomputable instance vkModule (K M : Type*) [Field K] [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℤ M] :
    Module K (VK K M) := (swapAdd K M).module K
noncomputable def swap (K M : Type*) [Field K] [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℤ M] :
    VK K M ≃ₗ[K] TensorProduct ℤ K M :=
  (swapAdd K M).linearEquiv K
noncomputable def F (K : Type*) {M : Type*} [Field K] [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℤ M]
    (f : Module.End ℤ M) : Module.End K (TensorProduct ℤ K M) := f.baseChange K
noncomputable def ind (K : Type*) {M : Type*} [Field K] [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℤ M]
    (f : Module.End ℤ M) : Module.End K (VK K M) :=
  (swap K M).symm.toLinearMap ∘ₗ F K f ∘ₗ (swap K M).toLinearMap
noncomputable def T (K : Type*) {M : Type*} [Field K] [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℤ M]
    (XM YM : ℕ → Module.End ℤ M) (ell : ℕ)
    (i j : Fin (ell + 1)) : Module.End K (TensorProduct ℤ K M) :=
  (c ell j : K)⁻¹ • F K (A XM YM ell i j)
def MatrixUnits {k : Type*} [Field k] {U : Type*} [AddCommGroup U] [Module k U]
    (n : ℕ) (t : Fin n → Fin n → Module.End k U) : Prop :=
  (∀ i j a b, t i j * t a b = if j = a then t i b else 0) ∧
  (∑ j, t j j) = 1
end Reduction
types: Nat.Prime p
CharP K p
0 ≤ lambda ∧ lambda < (p : ℤ)

FiniteDimensional ℂ V ∧ (Module.finrank ℂ V : ℤ) = lambda + 1 ∧ Nontrivial V ∧
(∀ W : Submodule ℂ V, YuiBasisObjects.Stable W x → YuiBasisObjects.Stable W y →
 YuiBasisObjects.Stable W h → W = ⊥ ∨ W = ⊤) ∧
(∃ w : V, w ≠ 0 ∧ x w = 0 ∧ h w = (lambda : ℂ) • w)
h * x - x * h = (2 : ℂ) • x ∧ h * y - y * h = (-2 : ℂ) • y ∧ x * y - y * x = h
v ≠ 0 ∧ x v = 0 ∧ h v = (lambda : ℂ) • v

(∃ (I : Type uV) (bZ : Module.Basis I ℤ M) (bC : Module.Basis I ℂ V),
 ∀ i, (bZ i : V) = bC i) ∧
(∀ (r : ℕ) (m : M), (XM r m : V) = YuiBasisObjects.dividedPower x r (m : V)) ∧
(∀ (r : ℕ) (m : M), (YM r m : V) = YuiBasisObjects.dividedPower y r (m : V))

∀ (K M : Type*) [Field K] [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℤ M], ∃ F : Module.End ℤ M →+* Module.End K (TensorProduct ℤ K M), ∀ (f : Module.End ℤ M) (a : K) (m : M), F f (TensorProduct.tmul ℤ a m) = TensorProduct.tmul ℤ a (f m)

1: # Typed interface and transition IR, versions 1 and 2
2: 
3: Version 1 remains readable without rewriting historical inputs. Version 2 adds
4: explicit object views and reviewed shared exports; it does not change NL0's
5: mathematical authority. This is Yui's implemented translation module.
6: 
7: ## Two layers of authority
8: 
9: The authoritative NL0 and Audit A are immutable within a translation run.
10: A translation-entry extraction may produce a separately versioned source under
11: [the local revision protocol](source-refactoring.md), never overwrite the old
12: authority. Its actual scoped reviews and unchanged baseline are combined by
13: source_preparation.py; a worksheet alone cannot establish acceptance. After source selection and
14: acceptance, an IR is a derived artifact:
15: 
16: 1. An **interface contract** fixes source/packet hashes, toolchain, shared
17:    Lean definitions, parameters, exact direct premises, the conclusion and the
18:    correspondence of these expressions with NL0. Creating this contract is
19:    formalization work, not free preprocessing. Normal entry requires actual independent semantic review before freeze.
20:    Final machine Audit B checks preservation of that reviewed encoding plus
21:    complete proof integrity. Exact strings alone cannot establish source fidelity.
22: 2. A **transition plan** maps NL0 paragraphs to typed local obligations with
23:    explicit inputs. It binds the interface-contract hash. Each obligation is
24:    a proposition under the shared parameter types and only its listed inputs.
25:    Its proof is a separate artifact. A well-typed plan can still be false.
26: 
27: The core transition engine consumes a frozen interface contract. A fresh model
28: or human may author this interface from the accepted NL0, explicit representation
29: choices and library tools. The normal pre-proof reviewer compares source and complete E/P types/definitions.
30: Final machine Audit B inherits that authority only if actual native evidence
31: preserves it. The lower-level compatibility path may record `PENDING_AUDIT_B`;
32: that path still requires actual semantic review and does not satisfy normal admission. Internal regression fixtures
33: also contain prepared interfaces for deterministic controls. Those fixtures and
34: their reference ports are never model-visible inputs to a mathematical test.
35: Reports include interface authoring/review costs; unmeasured owner work is labeled.
36: Legacy extracts do not inherit current Audit A status.
37: 
38: ## Contract file
39: 
40: `contract.json` contains `version: 1` or `2`, `id`, `source` (relative file and SHA256),
41: `source_steps` (the fragment's complete NL argument), `pins`, `header`,
42: `parameters` (`name`, `type`), `premises` (`id`, `type`, `kind`, `statement`),
43: `conclusion` (`statement`, `type`), `representation` and `review`. New whole-source
44: authors also supply `endpoint_correspondence`: a short direct/equivalent
45: explanation for each E and P, including all target hypotheses. Older contracts
46: may omit these notes; postprocessing then supplies them without editing proofs.
47: `header` holds the frozen imports/definitions selected during interface authoring;
48: proof workers cannot edit it. `review` records reviewer/exposure and pending issues;
49: it cannot grant Audit A/B. `representation` records equality/convergence mode,
50: norm/range, measure, representative and normalization choices when relevant.
51: 
52: Parameter records may additionally specify `binder_kind: explicit|implicit|instance`,
53: defaulting to `explicit`. This renders `(x : X)`, `{x : X}`, or `[x : X]`
54: respectively, so an arbitrary field/space can supply its legitimate typeclass
55: data in the Lean context. Binder style is preserved through types, assembly,
56: shared-proof keys and Audit B signatures. It supplies no new mathematical
57: assumption: the corresponding field/structure prerequisites still need exact
58: source correspondence review. Ordinary existing contracts retain their default.
59: 
60: `premises` contain project H/E inputs and optional M discharge ports, not extra
61: unproved facts. New translations can apply any pinned Mathlib result directly,
62: without an M port or permission record. In a
63: multi-node package, an N port is resolved by its actual upstream declaration.
64: Within one fragment, a conditional result may retain its declared N port, but
65: the report must say that the larger proof was not assembled. Definitions must
66: be fully supplied in the frozen header; existence guards remain premises.
67: 
68: ## Plan file
69: 
70: `plan.json` contains the contract's `version`, `contract_sha256`, `representation_notes`,
71: `steps` and `terminal`. Each step has `id` (`Tddd`), `statement` (Lean Prop),
72: `inputs` (direct premise IDs or other T IDs), `source_steps` (NL paragraph IDs)
73: and `explanation`. The terminal statement must equal the frozen Lean conclusion.
74: Every step must reach terminal and every source paragraph must be covered.
75: The dependency graph must be acyclic. Full source text is retained; a hash or
76: paragraph ID is not a replacement for mathematical content.
77: 
78: Version 2 optionally adds `objects` to the contract. Each object has an Oddd ID,
79: a complete mathematical `definition` and named `views` with Vddd IDs,
80: `lean_type` and `meaning`. Identity is global; views are selected per step with
81: `representations: [{object, view, expression}]`. The frozen types-only gate
82: checks each expression against its declared Lean type under that step's inputs.
83: Semantic fidelity is still separately reviewed. Nodes may also record
84: `bridges: [{object, from, to, input, explanation}]`; every bridge provider must
85: be an actual direct input. Records cannot replace the bridge proof.
86: The input's complete proposition determines what the bridge actually supplies:
87: it may transport a particular equality/property without asserting a general
88: isomorphism or a conversion in both directions. Check that narrower role in the
89: correspondence review; matching two view IDs is not a semantic proof.
90: 
91: The prototype keeps a fixed cross-node parameter context. Different internal
92: views may be defined locally. It does not yet synthesize arbitrary per-node
93: parameter adapters. [Shared lemmas](shared-lemmas.md) specify frozen exports,
94: permissions, exact reuse keys, physical storage and invalidation.
95: 
96: The prototype uses exact text for terminal interface identity after whitespace
97: normalization. Equivalent reformulations require a proved bridge or a reviewed
98: new contract version. This conservative constraint is an implementation choice,
99: not a claim that mathematical equivalence is textual equality.
100: 
101: ## Generated Lean
102: 
103: Each T becomes a standalone conditional theorem. Only its declared input
104: proofs are binders. It cannot see another T declaration during local checking.
105: The generated final P applies the actual local theorems in topological order
106: and discharges every T input. No `sorry`, auxiliary axiom, project predicate,
107: unproved instance or placeholder module is generated at any stage.
108: 
109: The initial implementation supports ordinary Lean Prop obligations under a
110: fixed context, not dependent witness export or arbitrary tactic-state mutation.
111: Package witnesses in an existential/structure statement; projections and
112: existence-dependent definitions need explicit contracts. Such packaging cannot
113: add fields holding results absent from the original theorem.
114: 
115: ## Parallel execution and invalidation
116: 
117: All local proof bodies may be developed concurrently after the contract and
118: plan interfaces are frozen: an input T is a local theorem parameter, not an
119: axiom. Mathematical dependencies govern final assembly, not necessarily worker
120: launch order. Shared definition changes invalidate every affected interface;
121: statement/input changes invalidate their downstream closure. Version 1 binds
122: the entire contract/plan hash conservatively. Cached results with stale hashes
123: must fail before compilation.
124: 
125: The current `scheduler.py` executes bodies within one graph concurrently,
126: including mathematically dependent conditional bodies, after a typecheck gate.
127: It records actual start/end intervals and assembles the real proofs. Shared
128: exports can be sourced from an explicit checked source store. `run_graph.py`
129: defaults to `max_concurrency=auto`, resolving to the frozen T-node count.
130: Earlier local Audit A reviews independently default to their current R-node count.
131: An explicit positive N caps each separate local phase. All local model stages share their case's ledger;
132: other cases own separate budgets. Python coordination consumes no model slot.
133: Free slots take the next queued node with a fresh model context. See
134: [the execution protocol](execution-protocol.md) for records, stops and ownership.
135: Queue intervals and observed
136: peak are recorded separately from requested bounds. Bank access is
137: disabled by default and optional when enabled. Historical 0.4 runs still used
138: sequential bodies and must retain that interpretation.
139: 
140: ## Status boundary
141: 
142: - `IR-STRUCTURE-PASSED`: explicit format, binding and graph checks only.
143: - `IR-TYPES-CHECKED`: Lean elaborated all local proposition types.
144: - `LOCAL-PROOF-CHECKED`: a named conditional T proof compiled.
145: - `FRAGMENT-ASSEMBLED`: all local proofs and the fixed P compiled together,
146:   with only the reported fragment premises and kernel foundation axioms.
147: - `SEMANTIC-REVIEWED`: the named reviewer inspected target/input/route
148:   correspondence; disclose owner/reference exposure and unresolved items.
149: 
150: None is a new whole-case Audit A/B or evidence of acceleration.
151: [Audit B](audit-b.md) independently checks every external statement and the
152: complete target (including hypotheses) against actual Lean types and relevant
153: definitions, guided by concise author explanations. Pinned Mathlib results are
154: freely available; no imported-theorem permission ledger is required. Fresh
155: assembly and root trust inspection remain necessary. Earlier fragment checks
156: have not retrospectively passed the changed policy. A complete generic Lean
157: repository adapter and Audit C/NL1 reconstruction remain outside Yui.
158: 
159: ## Accepted background supplement
160: 
161: The source authority includes verified node-local Audit A background notes.
162: Bind its supplement hash in `contract.source.background_supplement_sha256`
163: before interface freeze. New contracts use `source.background_mode:
164: node_local_reference`: original M references remain available, but notes are node-local
165: implementation references rather than extra typed premise ports. Elementary
166: notes inform local Lean work. Legacy contracts retain `promoted_inputs`.
167: Do not create new assumptions or forget notes when constructing task packets.
168: Audit B requires actual Lean closure; these notes do not restrict Mathlib use.
169: 
170: The interface source also retains the complete `background_supplement`, not
171: just its hash. Plan steps list the relevant qualified note IDs, for example
172: `background_notes:["R004.BG001"]`. Workflow freeze checks the paragraph mapping;
173: local Lean packets receive only their selected notes.
174: 
175: Canonical packets retain those complete notes. The Yui proof carrier projects
176: them to a compact local index in its initial prompt and supplies a scoped
177: `read_background_note` tool for full readback. Source/plan bindings and local reference isolation remain in place. The versioned access policy is
178: `local-background-on-demand-1`, recorded by translation carrier `yui-0.1.1`;
179: it is not retroactively attributed to old runs or pooled with their timing.
